project: Multi-Agent AI-Based Autonomous Path Planning and Obstacle Avoidance Robot
mission: Build a two-wheeled autonomous robot controlled by an Arduino Uno R3. The robot uses an HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor mounted on an MG995 servo to detect obstacles. An L298N driver controls the two DC motors. A Python-based multi-agent system generates the hardware architecture and firmware, while the navigation system plans and replans routes.

functional_requirements.text: Drive the left and right DC motors independently through the L298N motor driver.
Measure the distance to obstacles using the HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor.
Stop both motors when an obstacle is detected within the configured safety distance.
Control the MG995 servo to position the ultrasonic sensor for directional scanning.
Receive movement commands and transmit robot telemetry through USB serial communication.
Stop the motors when sensor measurements or incoming control commands are invalid.

non_functional_requirements.text: The control loop shall use non-blocking millis()-based timing.
Ultrasonic measurements shall be separated by at least 60 ms.
All controller-connected digital signals shall remain within the Arduino Uno 5 V logic limits.
Firmware shall use Arduino AVR-compatible APIs and compile for Arduino Uno R3.
The generated firmware shall use only the validated architecture pin map.

hardware_requirements.purpose: Independent direction and speed control of two DC motors.
Directional positioning of the ultrasonic sensor.

hardware_requirements.part: Two-wheel robot chassis with DC gear motors

acceptance_tests.given: the robot is powered and the motor driver is enabled
acceptance_tests.when: a forward movement command is received
acceptance_tests.then: both motors rotate in the forward direction.

acceptance_tests.given: an obstacle is detected within the configured safety distance
acceptance_tests.when: the next valid distance measurement is processed
a servo scan command is received
acceptance_tests.then: the MG995 moves to the requested scan position.

acceptance_tests.given: the robot is connected to the computer over USB
the ultrasonic sensor returns no valid echo
acceptance_tests.then: the motors remain stopped or enter the configured fail-safe state.

assumptions: Arduino Uno R3 is the primary controller.
The MG995 uses a separate regulated 5-6 V supply with adequate current capacity.
The L298N motor supply is selected according to the actual DC motor ratings.
The motor driver, controller and servo supply share a common ground.
The exact battery configuration has not yet been confirmed.
Wheel encoders and an IMU are not currently confirmed, so precise odometry is not assumed.
USB serial is used for the initial computer-to-robot communication.
open_questions: What are the rated voltage and stall current of the DC gear motors?
What battery and regulator configuration will be used?
What scan angles should be used for left, front and right obstacle measurements?
What movement command protocol should the Python navigation system use?
